subject: Billing/packaging question: heartbeat offset & minimums for hybrid sessions
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightcart.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@brightcart.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: question on heartbeat offset / minimums in draft SOW

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the SOW — Priya and I reviewed the packaging section this morning. Two billing items we wanted to confirm before we get legal to sign:

1) Heartbeat/prefix offset: Our app keeps an ephemeral prefix open between user sessions (300–1200 tokens average). The SOW references a 1-minute heartbeat window that counts as an active conversation for minimums. Can you confirm whether that heartbeat is charged as a full minimum (e.g., 1 min -> 1 unit) or prorated against the session bucket? We want to understand how many micro-sessions will convert into minimums when users bounce rapidly.

2) Rounding for fractional tokens: We saw the clause about token rounding to the nearest 10-token quantum. If we have streams of 7–12 token model calls during quick interactions, does each call round up individually, or can those be coalesced into a single billing window for rounding?

If you can share a short worked example (three quick requests of 9, 11, 8 tokens within 45s) that shows the invoice math we’d appreciate it — helps our finance folks.

Attached the latest SOW draft (BrightCart_MCP_draft.docx).

Best,
Alex
Head of Integrations, BrightCart

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: question on heartbeat offset / minimums in draft SOW

Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Logan (billing ops) and Vanessa (AM) so we can give a concrete example and propose clean language for the SOW.

Short answers up front:
- Heartbeat: treated as active-session time that can be amortized into an existing session bucket when the prefix is reused within the configured session window. It is not automatically a separate full minimum unless there is no active session to attach it to.
- Token rounding: rounding is computed on the billing aggregation window (not per RPC) so adjacent short calls within the same window can coalesce before applying the quantum.

I’ll leave the math and definitive SOW wording to Logan — tagging him for both the worked example and a suggested clause.

— Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightcart.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: question on heartbeat offset / minimums in draft SOW

Alex/Priya — thanks, here’s a concise worked example plus recommended SOW language. I attached an xlsx with the same math (sample-invoice-heartbeat-math.xlsx).

Worked example (system settings for BrightCart pilot):
- Billing quantum: 10 tokens
- Session minimum floor: 1 active-minute bucket (equivalent to 1 session-unit) if a session is not otherwise matched to an existing active bucket.
- Session aggregation window (heartbeat threshold): 90 seconds (we can set this per-customer; SOW currently says 60s — we can change it).

Scenario: three quick calls inside 45 seconds with raw token lengths 9, 11, 8.
Step 1 — token rounding (aggregation window): we aggregate calls that occur within the 90s window before applying the 10-token quantum. Aggregate tokens = 9 + 11 + 8 = 28 tokens.
Step 2 — apply quantum rounding: 28 rounded up to nearest 10-token quantum = 30 tokens billed.
Step 3 — convert to billing units: if the model SKU bills per 1,000-token block, then 30 tokens are 0.03 of that block (invoice shows fractional use).

Heartbeat behavior:
- If a heartbeat occurs and there is an existing active session bucket (within 90s), the heartbeat token usage and duration are merged into that bucket and do not trigger a separate minute minimum.
- If the heartbeat is isolated (no other calls in the 90s window), the platform will record an active-minute bucket which may hit the session minimum depending on configured minimums. In practice for BrightCart (300–1200 token prefixes) we recommend increasing the aggregation window to 120s to reduce false minimums for short-lived users.

Suggested SOW clause (short):
"Heartbeat and session minimums: Token rounding and minimums are computed over the configured session aggregation window (default 90s). Calls and heartbeats within the same aggregation window are coalesced for token-quantum rounding. An isolated heartbeat that cannot be attached to an existing active session may be billed as a session-minute minimum. Customer and Redwood may adjust aggregation window by mutual agreement in the SOW annex"

Let me know if you prefer the window tweaked to 120s — I’ll update the SOW wording and recalc the sample invoice.

Cheers,
Logan
Billing Ops Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightcart.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@brightcart.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Re: question on heartbeat offset / minimums in draft SOW

Thanks Logan — that example helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

1) On the aggregation window: BrightCart prefers 120s — our UX pattern has short re-activation bursts around 60–90s but extending to 120s will materially reduce the number of orphaned-heartbeat minimums. Please update SOW language to call out 120s as the default for our pilot.

2) On invoicing visibility: Can you add an invoice line example showing the three quick calls aggregated into 30 billed tokens, and separately show an example where an isolated heartbeat triggers a 1-minute session minimum (so our finance team can see both cases)?

3) On rounding thresholds: will coalescing across RPCs introduce any anti-abuse risk (e.g., accidentally coalescing very large numbers of tiny calls)? If so, can we add a cap (e.g., coalescing limited to 5 calls or a maximum of N tokens) so both sides are comfortable?

If you can push an updated SOW paragraph + two mini invoice line samples and the updated xlsx we’ll route to legal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex

From: logan_wright@redwood.ai <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@brightcart.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: question on heartbeat offset / minimums in draft SOW

Alex — agreed on 120s default for the pilot. I updated the XLSX and the SOW paragraph (attached in my reply). Summary of changes and answers: 

- Default aggregation window set to 120s for pilot (SOW annex).
- Invoice examples: included two sample lines — (A) aggregated RPCs -> 30 billed tokens; (B) isolated heartbeat -> 1 minute session minimum (represented as 1 session-unit line item). See file sample-invoice-heartbeat-math.xlsx (tab "samples").
- Anti-abuse cap: we propose a coalescing cap of either 5 calls or 1,000 tokens per aggregation window (whichever comes first). This prevents accidental aggregation of high-volume micro-RPC streams and is reflected in the proposed SOW wording: 

"Coalescing limit: coalescing for quantum rounding is limited to a maximum of 5 calls and 1,000 tokens per aggregation window to prevent undue aggregation of high-volume microcalls. Calls exceeding these caps will be billed in additional aggregation groups as necessary."

- Next steps: I’ll push an updated SOW paragraph to the HubSpot deal and attach the revised XLSX. Vanessa — can you confirm we’re comfortable with the 5-call / 1,000-token cap as a negotiable term?

If that all looks good I’ll send the DocuSign link for signature.

Thanks — Logan
